history.dynasty: Maratha Empire — Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Satara
history.period: 1713–1738 (present structure); Kavalem village bequeathed by Peshwa Baji Rao I in 1738; renovated 1966
history.summary: CSV town CORRECTED: the famous Shree Shantadurga Temple is NOT in Panaji — it stands at the foothill of Kavalem village, Ponda taluka, about 30 km from Panaji. The original temple at Quelossim (Keloshi) in Salcete was destroyed by the Portuguese in 1566; the goddess was shifted to Kavalem and worshipped in a small laterite-mud shrine. The present temple was constructed between 1713 and 1738 during the reign of Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj of Satara through the efforts of his minister Naroram Rege Mantri (of Kochara village, Vengurla taluka), who obtained finances from Shahu; Shrimant Baji Rao I Peshwa bequeathed the village of Kavalem to the temple in 1738. Shantadurga (Santeri) is the Kuldevi of many Goud Saraswat Brahmin families; Shrimad Swamiji of Shri Kavale Math is the spiritual head of the Saunsthan. The devasthan completed its 450th year on 4 December 2016. The temple shows Indo-Portuguese architecture — pyramidal shikhara, Roman-arched windows, flat dome, Deepastambha, tank and agrashalas (guest houses). Entry of foreigners has been restricted by the temple (reportedly over dress and conduct). Note: several sources date the original destruction to 1566; a couple say 1564 — verify.

name: Shree Shantadurga Temple
town_description: Kavale (Kavalem) is a village in Ponda taluka of North Goa, set in the foothills of a mountain chain about 30 km from Panaji, best known for the Shree Shantadurga temple.

travel.airport: Dabolim (Goa International) Airport about 45 km; Manohar International Airport (Mopa) about 50 km.
travel.railway: Karmali station about 12 km; Thivim about 30 km.
travel.road: About 30 km from Panaji via Ponda on the Kapileswari–Kavlem road; reachable by taxi and bus.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; the annual Jatra around Magh Shuddha Panchami (December/January) is the peak.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 6:00 AM to 8:30 PM daily on the temple's place listing — verify before visiting. Dress modestly; photography may be restricted inside.
